text:
Dose.ca called Zachary Bolduc "the unsung hero of the Canadiens," and the five-on-five numbers back it up. With the Trois-Rivieres native on the ice, Montreal takes 61.1% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), about 13 points better than when he sits. For a 23-year-old who came over from St. Louis, that's a winger making his line better, not just riding it.

He was cleared to play against Philadelphia on Nov. 21 and, now on the second power-play unit, scored from the slot off an Alex Newhook feed, per The Hockey News' Karine Hains. That makes 7 goals and 10 points in 24 games. He's shooting 17.1%, above the 13.5% our numbers expect, so a little of the goal total is finishing luck, but his own chances are solid. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking found a signature last season: 21% of his setups went across the royal road, against 7% for a typical forward. Evolving-Hockey credited him with 2.2 goals from penalties alone, drawing more than he takes. Our numbers project about 36 points.
headline: Zachary Bolduc, Montreal's quiet driver
